CLINICAL FEATURES OF MEASLES
Clinical Features
- The essential lesion is found on the skin, mucous membranes of the nasopharynx, bronchi, intestinal tract and conjunctivae
Three stages: Incubation period, prodromal stage with an exanthem and final stage
- Incubation period: Mild fever; 10 - 11 days
- Prodromal stage: 3 - 5 days
  · Low to moderate grade fever
  · Dry cough
  · Coryza
  · Conjunctivitis
  · Koplik spots
  · Photophobia
- Final stage: Temperature rises abruptly as the rash appears. Rash begins from the upper lateral part of the neck, behind the ears, along the hairline and posterior parts of the cheek then spreads to the rest of the body. Rash fades in the same pattern in 3 - 4 days. Associated lymphadenopathy
